title: PRD: Operational exit criteria and runbook tests for deterministic fallback behavior
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: After the regional cache-ejection incident on 2025-09-12, the postmortem recommended codifying deterministic fallback activation, a repeatable operational exit criteria, and automated runbook tests that validate fallback correctness and service-level impact. This ticket updates the PRD to include concrete requirements, acceptance tests, rollout constraints, and monitoring needs so that engineering and on-call teams can reliably trigger, verify, and roll back fallbacks without ambiguity. The goal is to reduce manual incident resolution time and prevent regressions by baking verification into the release gate.
scope: 1) Define objective exit criteria for automated and manual fallback triggers (latency, error-rate, queue-depth thresholds). 2) Specify deterministic simulation harnesses that can run in staging to exercise fallback paths and model-variant substitutions. 3) Create a set of runbook-driven synthetic tests (integration + smoke) that run pre- and post-deployment. 4) Define dashboard widgets and alerting rules to reflect fallback health and canary verification. 5) Specify ownership, operational playbook steps, and communication channels for fallback activation and rollback.
out_of_scope: Full redesign of the routing policy engine, long-term kernel-selection rework, and on-prem automated upgrades; those remain separate eng initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: Exit criteria are documented as numeric thresholds (e.g., p99 latency > X ms sustained for Y minutes, tail error-rate > Z% over 5m) and approved by SRE and runtime leads.
A staging simulation harness exists that can deterministically trigger the exact fallback code-paths used in production and produce a pass/fail report within 30 minutes.
Runbook tests (three scenarios: traffic surge, model variant OOM, and cross-region latency spike) are automated in CI and pass in staging with documented artifacts linked in the PRD.
Console shows a 'fallback health' dashboard with token-level cost delta, latency distribution, and SLO impact; alerts map to on-call rotations with runbook links.

A pre-flight checklist (rollout gate) that includes running the simulation harness, verifying synthetic checks, and security sign-off is required for any runtime-1.20 deployment that touches fallback code.
Security review completed and any KMS/HSM integration notes are captured; security gating does not block rollout if mitigations are listed and accepted.
Post-deployment smoke runs in production for 15 minutes with automated verification; if verification fails, an automated rollback is initiated per deployment contract.
Owners for each step are assigned in the PRD and the on-call runbook is published to the incident page.
Acceptance tests are included in the release checklist and must be green for canary to proceed to global rollout.
deliverables: Updated PRD section 'Fallback Operational Contracts' with numeric exit criteria and rollback rules.
Simulation harness repo and documentation with example inputs and expected outputs.
Three automated runbook tests in CI that can be scheduled as part of pre-release verification.
Console dashboard tiles and alert rules configured in observability (with dashboard JSON linked).
Runbook page with step-by-step instructions and Slack/PagerDuty links.
success_metrics: Mean time to resolution (MTTR) for fallback-related incidents reduced by 40% within 3 months of rollout.
Number of manual intervention rollbacks due to ambiguous exit criteria reduced to <1/month.
Percentage of releases with green pre-flight simulation and runbook checks = 95% within two cycles.
False-positive automated rollbacks from verification checks < 0.5% of rollouts.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Simulation harness may not fully represent production traffic patterns. Mitigation: include real-traffic-derived traces in the harness and run periodic replay tests.
Risk: Runbook tests create noisy failures in staging. Mitigation: isolate test networks and tag test traffic; provide guard rails to avoid long-running throttles.
Risk: Security questions around key material when running scripted rollbacks. Mitigation: Security review and scoped KMS roles for the simulation and CI runners.
Risk: Added release friction. Mitigation: keep pre-flight simulation under 30 minutes and allow opt-out for emergency patches with post-deploy verification.
decisions: Decision: Use numeric exit thresholds for SLO-linked fallbacks instead of qualitative rules to reduce ambiguity.
Decision: Simulation harness will live under org/runtime-sim and be maintained by the runtime infra team with PM oversight.
Decision: Security review is required but will not gate emergency rollbacks; instead, exceptions are logged and reviewed post-facto.
open_questions: What exact p99 latency threshold is acceptable for model groups that differ widely in token-costs? (Action: runtime eng to provide cost-latency matrix by 2025-10-10).
Should canary verification be synchronous in deploy pipeline or run as post-deploy automated smoke? (Proposal: both — light synchronous check + deeper post-deploy).
Who will own the simulation harness SLAs and pager rotation? (Suggested: runtime infra on-call with a named escalation to platform reliability).
How to coordinate fallbacks that span Dedicated pools and Private deployments with different rollback constraints? (Needs legal/enterprise input).
